$comment: Brief-parse eval fixture (playbook §10). `text` is a real-world Indian client brief; `expected` is the exact output of the deterministic mock parser (services/llm/brief_mock.py) AND the contract shape the real provider is held to. Regenerate deliberately with fixtures/llm/brief-parse/_tools/generate.py and read the diff.

assumptions.reason: The brief did not say how many floors — G+1 is the most common fit for an Indian urban plot. Change it if the client wants otherwise.
Stilt parking was not mentioned — assumed none; turn it on for a tight plot.
A basement was not mentioned — assumed none.
No bedroom count was given — 3BHK is the most common Indian independent-house programme.
A kitchen was not mentioned — every home needs one, so we added it.
A living/dining space was not mentioned — added one; it is the heart of the plan.
Bathroom count was not stated — assumed one toilet per two bedrooms, minimum two.
A utility/wash area was not asked for but is standard alongside an Indian kitchen.
Vastu was not mentioned — left off; switch it on any time.
No budget was given — costing will use the city benchmark ₹/sqft until you add one.
Parking was not mentioned — one covered car space, which most city bye-laws require.
Family size was not mentioned — the room programme drives the plan either way.
